description:
Susan Huang’s talk highlights a fundamental shift from traditional "exchange logic", where loyalty was traded for stability, to a new "experience exchange" model centered on growth, connection, and meaning. Because the future is increasingly unpredictable, she argues that the present has become the primary currency, urging students to focus less on finding the "perfect" career choice and more on how they adapt and translate their experiences into transferable skills. Ultimately, in an era where lifetime employment no longer exists, the bond between individuals and their work is redefined by the immediate value of the journey rather than the promise of a destination. 

Susan Huang is an HR strategist with over 14 years of experience across APAC in luxury, real estate, and education. Specializing in talent acquisition and people strategy, she leverages dual Master’s degrees in intercultural education and communication to align organizational growth with human potential. title: How young people can find better jobs | Susan Huang | TEDxNYU Shanghai

description:
What if perfection isn't helping you succeed—but quietly keeping you stuck? In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, a simple drawing assignment with one surprising rule becomes the starting point for a bigger conversation about perfectionism, unfinished goals, and the invisible habits that keep us from moving forward. Through personal stories and practical insights, this talk challenges us to rethink what it really means to make progress—and why sometimes the most powerful thing we can do is simply decide something is done. Born and raised in Johnson City, Tennessee, Alexandra is completing her undergraduate degree in Interior Architecture at East Tennessee State University.

As Director of Young Professionals On Campus (YPOC), she connects students with the broader Johnson City community through events, mentorship, and partnerships that create meaningful relationships and real opportunities. title: There Are No Erasers in Life | Alexandra Battle | TEDxJohnsonCity

description: Most people spend years trying to perfect one craft. After an 11-year career as a professional ballerina with The Royal Ballet in London, Beatriz Stix-Brunell mastered one of the world's most demanding—then walked away to start over as a Stanford student. What does it mean to start a new life, and how might we approach it in a way that stretches our vision of possibility? Beatriz knows firsthand the demands of mastering a discipline and how to apply the rigor and skills of a past life towards a new direction. Prior to coming to Stanford to pursue her undergraduate degree in Symbolic Systems, Beatriz had an 11-year career as a professional ballerina with The Royal Ballet in London. For over two decades, her day-to-day consisted of rigorous training in a high performance environment. title: Pivot Pointes: Center Stage to Starting Over | Beatriz Stix-Brunell | TEDxStanford

description: In this powerful TEDx talk, Milan Bavishi (Director of Content at Upstox) breaks down why our traditional playbook "study hard, plan carefully, eliminate risk" fails in an unpredictable world. From the 2008 global financial crisis to the 2020 pandemic, Milan shares the three crucial mindset shifts every student, engineer, and entrepreneur needs to turn uncertainty from a threat into a competitive edge. Milan is a stock market expert with over two decades of experience in the equity markets. He has established himself as a trusted authority in trading and investing. His passion for simplifying complex financial concepts and empowering individuals has made him a sought after educator and mentor. He currently works as Director, Content at Upstox. description:
The end of fear is often the beginning of possibility. This talk invites audiences to challenge self-doubt, embrace uncertainty, and discover how courage can transform obstacles into opportunities. Nasreen Abdulla is a seasoned journalist with over 18 years of experience across broadcast, print, and digital platforms. As a Special Correspondent at Khaleej Times, the UAE’s first English-language newspaper, Nasreen has covered some of the region’s most important and human-centered stories—from reporting at the Rafah border on the UAE’s humanitarian mission for injured Palestinian children, to exploring the future of transport in Dubai through the groundbreaking Loop project, and unpacking key moments at the Dubai-India Business Summit.

She has also ventured into radio, TV, and digital media. Alongside her busy career, Nasreen is an enthusiastic fitness and hiking aficionado. Over the past five years, she has achieved certification as a fitness trainer and earned a purple belt in Jiu Ji

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What makes a substance ethical or unethical? Dr Marianne Jauncey challenges our unconscious biases about drug use and the hypocrisy in how we regulate mind-altering substances. Drawing on decades of experience working with people who inject drugs, she explores how harm, medical utility and social outcomes should inform our understanding of drug ethics. Dr Jauncey has been Medical Director of the Uniting MSIC since 2008. She has worked many years in the drug and alcohol field & holds her Masters in Public Health. She is also a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at the National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre UNSW and a Clinical Senior Lecturer at the University of Sydney’s Medical School.

Passionate about making a difference to the wider community, her research interests include increasing access to hepatitis C treatment for injecting drug users, drug overdose and the physiological changes that occur after drug injection. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: The Hypocrisy Hangover | Marianne Jauncey | TEDxUNSW

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Every one of us eventually stands at a crossroads, be it choosing a career, a relationship, or a new direction in life. We believe these choices are entirely our own. But what if many of them are being quietly influenced by beliefs we never consciously chose?

In this talk, Geetika Dadwwaani explores how childhood conditioning, emotional experiences, and the deep human need for belonging shape our decisions long before we become aware of them. Through a deeply personal story, insights from neuroscience and psychology, and her practical belief rewiring framework, she challenges the audience to question inherited beliefs, strengthen self-worth, and make courageous, authentic choices.

"The Silent Algorithm" is ultimately a message of hope - our past may have written the first lines of our story, but we all have the power to rewrite the code that shapes our future." Geetika Dadwwaani's approach bridges ancient practices with
modern methodologies, enabling people to heal emotional wounds
title: The Silent Algorithm ! | Geetika Dadwwaani | TEDxThe NGP School Coimbatore
